_about: Story chapters (plan §4.2). 'facts' are short, owner-confirmed or verified lines that render as they are. The narrative for each chapter is imported from content/story/<id>.md when the copy track has written it; until then the page shows a PLACEHOLDER block (a release build fails on it). 'photo' is an id in photos.json.

chapters.title: Two Texans and a Gram Parsons song
facts: David Dewese and Chad Edgington wrote to each other through the winter and spring of 1997.
They chose the band’s name over spring break 1997, when they met up in Texas to record a stack of songs together on a 4-track.
The name comes from the Gram Parsons song “Luxury Liner”.
In May 1997 they moved to Nashville, the band’s home town from then on.

chapters.title: Powder-blue suits and the first recordings
facts: The first Nashville line-ups had Jeff LaFrate and then Kyle Edgington on drums, and Mark W. Winchester on bass.
Playing Billy Block’s Western Beat Roots Revival at Zanies in Nashville, probably in autumn 1997 or winter 1998, the band met Emmylou Harris and Phil Kaufman.
Scott Carpenter joined on drums in August 1998.
For its first full-band concert, at 12th & Porter in Nashville in July or August 1998, opening for Austin Hanks, the band wore suits by Manuel.
The band was featured in Billboard in 1998.
In autumn 1998 the band played the Texas Music Café in Waco, Texas: Chad on guitar, David on bass and Scott on drums.

chapters.title: Sound As Ever
facts: Sound As Ever came out in May 2000.
The album is named after Gram Parsons’s sign-off, “Sound as ever”.
David “Larry” Wilstermann joined on bass in December 2000.

chapters.title: Believe, SXSW and Chad’s last show
facts: The Believe EP came out in March 2001, with the band’s own “Shake It Up” and a cover of Cher’s “Believe”.
The band played the SESAC Showcase at SXSW 2001.
Chad Edgington played his last show with the band in March 2001 and left Nashville; David carried the band on as a trio with Scott and Larry.

chapters.title: The journal years
facts: The band kept a journal on its website from 2001 to 2004, logging shows from Memphis to Las Vegas.
In August 2002 the band opened for Blues Traveler in Atlanta.

chapters.title: Overbored
facts: Overbored came out in May 2003.
“Dreaming” was used in One Tree Hill, first aired on The WB on February 24, 2004.
“Sunshine” was the theme song of FOX Sports’ US Youth Soccer Show.

chapters.title: Nonetheless
facts: Nonetheless came out in October 2006. David Dewese wrote the songs.

chapters.title: The quiet years
facts: In 2008 Chad Edgington joined David on stage for a few songs at David’s solo CD-release show in Dallas.
The band slowly stopped touring and releasing music in the late 2000s, but the four never said it was over.

chapters.title: Great Day
facts: In 2021 the band released “Shake It Up (Live at the Texas Music Café)”, recorded live in Waco, Texas, in autumn 1998.
The band never broke up. The four forever members reconnected during the pandemic and started making music again.
“Great Day” (February 2026) and “New Beginning” (April 2026), both written by Chad Edgington and David Dewese, have all four forever members playing on them.
In 2026 Sound As Ever came out on vinyl for the first time.
